idiom_name: named constructor / factory function returning the aggregate by value (unique_ptr for polymorphic products)
implementation_notes: Modern C++ expresses the DDD factory as a named constructor: a static member or free function with a domain name that validates its input and returns the aggregate by value, or std::unique_ptr (std::make_unique, C++14) when the product is polymorphic; what replaces the classic factory class is the factory function plus a private/protected constructor, which makes bypass impossible in application code. The class-based Factory Method and Abstract Factory structures remain justified only when the creation policy itself must vary at run time, and the C++23 std::expected variant replaces exceptions with a value-based error channel.
pitfalls: Throwing from the factory unwinds through caller frames; in noexcept or hard-real-time code prefer the std::expected variant.
Returning a polymorphic product by value slices it - return std::unique_ptr<Base> and build it with std::make_unique instead.
A private constructor also hides the type from generic helpers (containers, std::make_shared); provide a factory entry point for those paths too.

variants.name: Factory function returning std::expected (no exceptions)
variants.implementation_notes: The same named-constructor shape with the failure returned as a value: return std::expected<Order, OrderError> and build the failure with std::unexpected, so callers chain with and_then/transform instead of catching. Choose it where the codebase builds without exceptions or where a creation failure is part of the domain's vocabulary; it needs a C++23 toolchain and a domain error type in place of exception classes.
pitfalls: Dereferencing a valueless std::expected is undefined behaviour and value() throws bad_expected_access; the error branch must be handled.
Mixing exception-based and expected-based factories in one codebase makes call sites inconsistent; choose one error channel per module boundary.
